steps.text: # A2A Protocol Agent2Agent Protocol Logo ------------------------- An open protocol enabling communication and interoperability between opaque agentic applications. An open standard enabling users to connect agents to tools and data through MCP, and to other agents through A2A. An open standard enabling developers to expose portable tools through MCP and interoperable agents through A2A. What is A2A Protocol?[¶](#what-is-a2a-protocol "Permanent link") ---------------------------------------------------------------- The **Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol** is an open standard for seamless communication and collaboration between AI agents. In a world where agents are built using diverse frameworks and by different vendors, A2A provides the definitive common language for agent interoperability. Build with **[![ADK Logo](https://adk.dev/assets/agent-development-kit.png) ADK](https://adk.dev/)** *(or any framework)*, equip with **[![MCP Logo](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/mcp.png) MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)** *(or any tool)*, and communicate with **![A2A Logo](assets/a2a_logo/icon/color/SVG/a2a_icon_color.svg) A2A**, to remote agents, local agents, and humans. Key Features[¶](#key-features "Permanent link") ----------------------------------------------- * **Interoperability** Connect agents built on different platforms (LangGraph, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, custom solutions) to create powerful, composite AI systems. * **Complex Workflows** Enable agents to delegate sub-tasks, exchange information, and coordinate actions to solve complex problems that a single agent cannot. * **Secure & Opaque** Agents interact without needing to share internal memory, tools, or proprietary logic, ensuring security and preserving intellectual property. * **Extensible** Add capabilities through formal protocol [extensions and custom bindings](topics/extension-and-binding-governance/), governed by a tiered promotion process so the core stays stable. Get started with A2A[¶](#get-started-with-a2a "Permanent link") --------------------------------------------------------------- * **Read the Introduction** Understand the core ideas behind A2A. [What is A2A?](topics/what-is-a2a/) [Key Concepts](topics/key-concepts/) * **Dive into the Specification** Explore the detailed technical definition of the A2A protocol. [Protocol Specification](specification/) * **Follow the Tutorials** Build your first A2A-compliant agent with our step-by-step Python quickstart. [Hands-on-Tutorial](tutorials/python/1-introduction/) * **Explore Code Samples** See A2A in action with sample clients, servers, and agent framework integrations. [GitHub Samples](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-samples) * **Use the A2A CLI** Discover, message, and manage any A2A agent from your terminal — and give your coding assistant the same power. [Introducing the A2A CLI](blog/2026/10/01/introducing-a2a-cli/) [a2aproject/a2a-cli](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-cli) * **Download the Official SDKs** [Python](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-python) [JavaScript](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-js) [Java](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-java) [C#/.NET](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-dotnet) [Golang](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-go) [Rust](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-rs) * **Video** Intro in under 8 min * **Course** [DeepLearning.AI](https://www.deeplearning.ai/) - Intro to A2A [![A2A DeepLearning.AI](https://img.youtube.com/vi/4gYm0Rp7VHc/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://goo.gle/dlai-a2a) How A2A Works with MCP[¶](#how-a2a-works-with-mcp "Permanent link") ------------------------------------------------------------------- The Model Context Protocol (MCP) and the A2A Protocol are not competitors — they are highly complementary. They solve two different problems and are designed to work together. * **MCP is for agent-to-tool communication:** it standardizes how an agent connects to its tools, APIs, and resources to get information. See [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/). * **A2A is for agent-to-agent communication:** as a universal, decentralized standard, A2A lets independent agents — including those using MCP — discover each other, delegate tasks, and share results. Use MCP to equip an individual agent with the specific tools it needs to do its job (e.g., access to a GitHub repository or a SQL database). Use A2A to let that specialized agent securely collaborate with other agents across different frameworks. ``` flowchart LR User(🧑‍💻 User) <--> ClientAgent(🤖 Client Agent) RemoteAgent(🤖 Remote Agent) RemoteTool(⚙️ Remote Tool) ClientAgent -- Using --> RemoteAgent ClientAgent -- Using --> RemoteTool style User fill:#fdebd0,stroke:#e67e22,stroke-width:2px style ClientAgent fill:#d6eaf8,stroke:#3498db,stroke-width:2px style RemoteAgent fill:#d6eaf8,stroke:#3498db,stroke-width:2px style RemoteTool fill:#d6eaf8,stroke:#3498db,stroke-width:2px ``` *A client agent reaches remote tools with MCP and remote agents with A2A.* [A2A and MCP — deeper dive](topics/a2a-and-mcp/) What A2A Is Not[¶](#what-a2a-is-not "Permanent link") ----------------------------------------------------- A2A is a focused protocol. To set expectations, here is what it explicitly does not try to be: * **Not an agent development kit** like LangGraph, CrewAI, or ADK for building agentic applications. A2A is the communication layer between agents built with any of these. * **Not a sub-agent or tool-call protocol.** A2A does not specify how an agent talks to its own sub-agents or how it invokes tools — use your framework's native primitives, or MCP, for those. * **Not a replacement for [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/).** MCP standardizes agent-to-tool communication; A2A standardizes agent-to-agent communication. They are complementary (see [above](#how-a2a-works-with-mcp)). * **Not an interactive messaging app** like Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, or Telegram. A2A is a machine-to-machine protocol for autonomous agents. Governance & Open Source[¶](#governance-open-source "Permanent link") --------------------------------------------------------------------- A2A was originally developed by Google and donated to the Linux Foundation. It is maintained by a Technical Steering Committee with representatives from AWS, Cisco, Google, IBM Research, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP, and ServiceNow, and supported by a broad community of [partners](partners/). Join the community on [Discord](https://discord.gg/a2aprotocol) to connect with contributors, ask questions, and discuss the protocol. For details on how the project is run, see [`GOVERNANCE.md`](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md) and [`MAINTAINERS.md`](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md). License[¶](#license "Permanent link") ------------------------------------- The A2A Protocol is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/LICENSE) and welcomes [contributions](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) from the community.

1: # A2A and MCP - A2A Protocol
2: 
3: A2A and MCP: Detailed Comparison[¶](#a2a-and-mcp-detailed-comparison "Permanent link")
4: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5: 
6: In AI agent development, two key protocol types emerge to facilitate
7: interoperability. One connects agents to tools and resources. The other enables
8: agent-to-agent collaboration. The Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol and the
9: [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP) address these distinct but highly complementary needs.
10: 
11: Horizontal and Vertical Layers[¶](#horizontal-and-vertical-layers "Permanent link")
12: -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
13: 
14: One way to picture the two protocols is by the direction they connect in.
15: 
16: **MCP is vertical.** It deepens a single agent. You can build an agentic system
17: under one roof — one or more agents in a single application. Every MCP connection
18: you add hands an agent another tool, resource, or skill. The more you connect,
19: the more that agent can do on its own.
20: 
21: **A2A is horizontal.** It connects agents across that boundary. The other agent
22: may belong to another team, another department, or a partner organization. Your
23: agent reaches out to those agents to discover them, negotiate, and exchange
24: information.
25: 
26: That horizontal reach goes beyond asking another agent for a status update. It is
27: closer to how one person reaches out to another for help: *"Are you working on
28: this project? Do you know about it? Can you share what you have — and if not,
29: which agent can?"* Agents break the ice, exchange context, and — depending on how
30: the exchange goes — either go deeper or get pointed to a better place to get the
31: job done.
32: 
33: Used together, MCP gives each agent depth, and A2A gives your system reach.
34: 
35: Model Context Protocol[¶](#model-context-protocol "Permanent link")
36: -------------------------------------------------------------------
37: 
38: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) defines how an AI agent uses individual tools and resources, such as a database or an API.
39: 
40: This protocol offers the following capabilities:
41: 
42: * Standardizes how AI models and agents connect to and interact with tools,
43:   APIs, and other external resources.
44: * Defines a structured way to describe tool capabilities, similar to function
45:   calling in Large Language Models.
46: * Passes inputs to tools and receives structured outputs.
47: * Supports common use cases, such as an LLM calling an external API, an agent
48:   querying a database, or an agent connecting to predefined functions.
49: 
50: Agent2Agent Protocol[¶](#agent2agent-protocol "Permanent link")
51: ---------------------------------------------------------------
52: 
53: The Agent2Agent Protocol lets different agents collaborate to reach a common goal.
54: 
55: This protocol offers the following capabilities:
56: 
57: * Standardizes how independent, often opaque, AI agents communicate and
58:   collaborate as peers.
59: * Gives agents an application-level protocol. With it, agents discover each
60:   other and negotiate interactions. They also manage shared tasks and exchange
61:   conversational context and complex data.
62: * Supports common use cases. For example, a customer service agent might delegate
63:   an inquiry to a billing agent. A travel agent might coordinate with flight,
64:   hotel, and activity agents.
65: 
66: Why Different Protocols?[¶](#why-different-protocols "Permanent link")
67: ----------------------------------------------------------------------
68: 
69: Both protocols are essential for building complex AI systems. The distinction between A2A and MCP depends on what an agent interacts with.
70: 
71: * **Tools and Resources (MCP Domain)**:
72:   + **Characteristics:** These are typically primitives with well-defined,
73:     structured inputs and outputs. They perform specific, often stateless,
74:     functions. Examples include a calculator, a database query API, or a
75:     weather lookup service.
76:   + **Purpose:** Agents use tools to gather information and perform discrete
77:     functions.
78: * **Agents (A2A domain)**:
79:   + **Characteristics:** These are more autonomous systems. They reason,
80:     plan, and use multiple tools. They keep state over longer interactions
81:     and hold complex, often multi-turn dialogues to handle novel or evolving
82:     tasks.
83:   + **Purpose:** Agents collaborate with other agents to tackle broader, more
84:     complex goals.
85: 
86: A2A ❤️ MCP: Complementary Protocols for Agentic Systems[¶](#a2a-mcp-complementary-protocols-for-agentic-systems "Permanent link")
87: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
88: 
89: An agentic application might use A2A to communicate with other agents. Inside,
90: each agent uses MCP to work with its own tools and resources.
91: 
92: ![Diagram showing A2A and MCP working together. A User interacts with Agent A using A2A. Agent A interacts with Agent B using A2A. Agent B uses MCP to interact with Tool 1 and Tool 2.](../../assets/a2a-mcp.png)
93: 
94: *A2A connects the agents to each other; MCP connects each agent to its own tools.*
95: 
96: ### Example Scenario: The Auto Repair Shop[¶](#example-scenario-the-auto-repair-shop "Permanent link")
97: 
98: Consider an auto repair shop staffed by autonomous AI agent "mechanics".
99: These mechanics diagnose and repair problems with special-purpose tools. Their
100: tools include vehicle diagnostic scanners, repair manuals, and platform lifts.
101: The repair process can involve long conversations, research, and work with part
102: suppliers.
103: 
104: * **Customer interaction — user-to-agent via A2A.** A customer, or their
105:   assistant agent, talks to the "Shop Manager" agent.
106: 
107:   For example, the customer might say, "My car is making a rattling noise".
108: * **Diagnostic conversation — agent-to-agent via A2A.** The Shop Manager agent
109:   holds a back-and-forth diagnostic conversation.
110: 
111:   For example, the Manager might ask, "Can you send a video of the noise?" or "I see some fluid leaking. How long has this been happening?".
112: * **Internal tool use — agent-to-tool via MCP.** The Mechanic agent, assigned
113:   the task by the Shop Manager, needs to diagnose the issue. It uses MCP to
114:   reach its specialized tools.
115: 
116:   For example:
117: 
118:   + MCP call to a "Vehicle Diagnostic Scanner" tool:
119:     `scan_vehicle_for_error_codes(vehicle_id='XYZ123')`
120:   + MCP call to a "Repair Manual Database" tool:
121:     `get_repair_procedure(error_code='P0300', vehicle_make='Toyota',
122:     vehicle_model='Camry')`
123:   + MCP call to a "Platform Lift" tool: `raise_platform(height_meters=2)`
124: * **Supplier interaction — agent-to-agent via A2A.** The Mechanic agent finds
125:   that a specific part is needed. It uses A2A to talk to a "Parts Supplier"
126:   agent and order the part.
127:   For example, the
128:   Mechanic agent might ask, "Do you have part #12345 in stock for a Toyota Camry 2018?"
129: * **Order processing — agent-to-agent via A2A.** The Parts Supplier agent is
130:   also an A2A-compliant system. It responds, which can lead to an order.
131:

134: * A2A handles the higher-level, conversational, task-oriented interactions. It
135:   links the customer with the shop, and the shop's agents with outside supplier
136:   agents.
137: * MCP enables the mechanic agent to use its specific, structured tools to
138:   perform its diagnostic and repair functions.

# What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems.

Using MCP, AI applications like Claude or ChatGPT can connect to data sources (e.g. local files, databases), tools (e.g. search engines, calculators) and workflows (e.g. specialized prompts)—enabling them to access key information and perform tasks.

Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications. Just as USB-C provides a standardized way to connect electronic devices, MCP provides a standardized way to connect AI applications to external systems.

![](https://mintcdn.com/mcp/bEUxYpZqie0DsluH/images/mcp-simple-diagram.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=bEUxYpZqie0DsluH\&q=85\&s=35268aa0ad50b8c385913810e7604550)

## What can MCP enable?

* Agents can access your Google Calendar and Notion, acting as a more personalized AI assistant.
* Claude Code can generate an entire web app using a Figma design.
* Enterprise chatbots can connect to multiple databases across an organization, empowering users to analyze data using chat.
* AI models can create 3D designs on Blender and print them out using a 3D printer.

## Why does MCP matter?

Depending on where you sit in the ecosystem, MCP can have a range of benefits.

* **Developers**: MCP reduces development time and complexity when building, or integrating with, an AI application or agent.
* **AI applications or agents**: MCP gives them access to an ecosystem of data sources, tools and apps, which enhances their capabilities and improves the end-user experience.
* **End-users**: MCP results in more capable AI applications or agents that can access user data and take actions on the user's behalf when necessary.

## Broad ecosystem support

MCP is an open protocol supported across a wide range of clients and servers. AI assistants like [Claude](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building) and [ChatGPT](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/mcp/), development tools like [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers), [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp), [MCPJam](https://docs.mcpjam.com/getting-started), and many others all support MCP — making it easy to build once and integrate everywhere.

# Specification

[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) is an open protocol that
enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and
tools. Whether you're building an AI-powered IDE, enhancing a chat interface, or creating
custom AI workflows, MCP provides a standardized way to connect LLMs with the context
they need.

This specification defines the authoritative protocol requirements, based on the
TypeScript schema in
[schema.ts](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification/blob/main/schema/2025-06-18/schema.ts).

For implementation guides and examples, visit
[modelcontextprotocol.io](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD
NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be
interpreted as described in [BCP 14](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/bcp14)
\[[RFC2119](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2119)]
\[[RFC8174](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8174)] when, and only when, they
appear in all capitals, as shown here.

## Overview

MCP provides a standardized way for applications to:

* Share contextual information with language models
* Expose tools and capabilities to AI systems
* Build composable integrations and workflows

The protocol uses [JSON-RPC](https://www.jsonrpc.org/) 2.0 messages to establish
communication between:

* **Hosts**: LLM applications that initiate connections
* **Clients**: Connectors within the host application
* **Servers**: Services that provide context and capabilities

MCP takes some inspiration from the
[Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/), which
standardizes how to add support for programming languages across a whole ecosystem of
development tools. In a similar way, MCP standardizes how to integrate additional context
and tools into the ecosystem of AI applications.

## Key Details

### Base Protocol

* [JSON-RPC](https://www.jsonrpc.org/) message format
* Stateful connections
* Server and client capability negotiation

### Features

Servers offer any of the following features to clients:

* **Resources**: Context and data, for the user or the AI model to use
* **Prompts**: Templated messages and workflows for users
* **Tools**: Functions for the AI model to execute

Clients may offer the following features to servers:

* **Sampling**: Server-initiated agentic behaviors and recursive LLM interactions
* **Roots**: Server-initiated inquiries into uri or filesystem boundaries to operate in
* **Elicitation**: Server-initiated requests for additional information from users

### Additional Utilities

* Configuration
* Progress tracking
* Cancellation
* Error reporting
* Logging

## Security and Trust & Safety

The Model Context Protocol enables powerful capabilities through arbitrary data access
and code execution paths. With this power comes important security and trust
considerations that all implementors must carefully address.

### Key Principles

1. **User Consent and Control**
   * Users must explicitly consent to and understand all data access and operations
   * Users must retain control over what data is shared and what actions are taken
   * Implementors should provide clear UIs for reviewing and authorizing activities

2. **Data Privacy**
   * Hosts must obtain explicit user consent before exposing user data to servers
   * Hosts must not transmit resource data elsewhere without user consent
   * User data should be protected with appropriate access controls

3. **Tool Safety**
   * Tools represent arbitrary code execution and must be treated with appropriate
     caution.
     * In particular, descriptions of tool behavior such as annotations should be
       considered untrusted, unless obtained from a trusted server.
   * Hosts must obtain explicit user consent before invoking any tool
   * Users should understand what each tool does before authorizing its use

4. **LLM Sampling Controls**
   * Users must explicitly approve any LLM sampling requests
   * Users should control:
     * Whether sampling occurs at all
     * The actual prompt that will be sent
     * What results the server can see
   * The protocol intentionally limits server visibility into prompts

### Implementation Guidelines

While MCP itself cannot enforce these security principles at the protocol level,
implementors **SHOULD**:

1. Build robust consent and authorization flows into their applications
2. Provide clear documentation of security implications
3. Implement appropriate access controls and data protections
4. Follow security best practices in their integrations
5. Consider privacy implications in their feature designs

3: A2A and MCP: Detailed Comparison[¶](#a2a-and-mcp-detailed-comparison "Permanent link")
4: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5: 
6: In AI agent development, two key protocol types emerge to facilitate
7: interoperability. One connects agents to tools and resources. The other enables
8: agent-to-agent collaboration. The Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol and the
9: [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP) address these distinct but highly complementary needs.
10: 
11: Horizontal and Vertical Layers[¶](#horizontal-and-vertical-layers "Permanent link")
12: -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
13: 
14: One way to picture the two protocols is by the direction they connect in.
15: 
16: **MCP is vertical.** It deepens a single agent. You can build an agentic system
17: under one roof — one or more agents in a single application. Every MCP connection
18: you add hands an agent another tool, resource, or skill. The more you connect,
19: the more that agent can do on its own.
20: 
21: **A2A is horizontal.** It connects agents across that boundary. The other agent
22: may belong to another team, another department, or a partner organization. Your
23: agent reaches out to those agents to discover them, negotiate, and exchange
24: information.
25: 
26: That horizontal reach goes beyond asking another agent for a status update. It is
27: closer to how one person reaches out to another for help: *"Are you working on
28: this project? Do you know about it? Can you share what you have — and if not,
29: which agent can?"* Agents break the ice, exchange context, and — depending on how
30: the exchange goes — either go deeper or get pointed to a better place to get the
31: job done.
32: 
33: Used together, MCP gives each agent depth, and A2A gives your system reach.
34: 
35: Model Context Protocol[¶](#model-context-protocol "Permanent link")
36: -------------------------------------------------------------------
37: 
38: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) defines how an AI agent uses individual tools and resources, such as a database or an API.
39: 
40: This protocol offers the following capabilities:
41: 
42: * Standardizes how AI models and agents connect to and interact with tools,
43:   APIs, and other external resources.
44: * Defines a structured way to describe tool capabilities, similar to function
45:   calling in Large Language Models.
46: * Passes inputs to tools and receives structured outputs.
47: * Supports common use cases, such as an LLM calling an external API, an agent
48:   querying a database, or an agent connecting to predefined functions.
49: 
50: Agent2Agent Protocol[¶](#agent2agent-protocol "Permanent link")
51: ---------------------------------------------------------------
52: 
53: The Agent2Agent Protocol lets different agents collaborate to reach a common goal.
54: 
55: This protocol offers the following capabilities:
56: 
57: * Standardizes how independent, often opaque, AI agents communicate and
58:   collaborate as peers.
59: * Gives agents an application-level protocol. With it, agents discover each
60:   other and negotiate interactions. They also manage shared tasks and exchange
61:   conversational context and complex data.
62: * Supports common use cases. For example, a customer service agent might delegate
63:   an inquiry to a billing agent. A travel agent might coordinate with flight,
64:   hotel, and activity agents.
65: 
66: Why Different Protocols?[¶](#why-different-protocols "Permanent link")
67: ----------------------------------------------------------------------
68: 
69: Both protocols are essential for building complex AI systems. The distinction between A2A and MCP depends on what an agent interacts with.
70: 
71: * **Tools and Resources (MCP Domain)**:
72:   + **Characteristics:** These are typically primitives with well-defined,
73:     structured inputs and outputs. They perform specific, often stateless,
74:     functions. Examples include a calculator, a database query API, or a
75:     weather lookup service.
76:   + **Purpose:** Agents use tools to gather information and perform discrete

**互操作性：跨框架的组合系统。** A2A 使构建在不同平台上的 agent 能够彼此连接，官方文档明确列出 LangGraph、CrewAI、Semantic Kernel 及自定义方案等目标，从而组合出强大的复合 AI 系统[S1]。这避免了厂商锁定的碎片化，让异构 agent 在同一声明中互通。

**复杂工作流：委派、信息交换与协调行动。** A2A 支持 agent 委派子任务、交换信息并协调行动，以解决单个 agent 无法单独应对的复杂问题[S1]。协议落实到操作层面，可标准化多个独立、通常不透明的 AI agent 以对等方身份通信与协作；在应用级协议上赋予 agent 相互发现、协商交互、管理共享任务以及交换对话上下文与复杂数据的能力，并天然覆盖客户服务、旅行调度等常见场景[S4]。

**安全与不透明：兼顾安全与知识产权。** agent 之间的交互无需共享内部记忆、工具或专有逻辑，从而在协作的同时维护安全并保护知识产权[S1]。这意味着协作可以在不暴露各自实现细节的前提下进行，是面向跨组织边界的务实设计。

**可扩展：核心稳定与能力增生。** agent 的能力可通过正式的协议扩展与自定义绑定来增加，并由分层的晋升机制加以治理，使得核心保持稳定[S1]。这种「扩展而不动摇核心」的工程机制，保证了协议在持续演化中的长期可用性。

综上，A2A 的创新体现在跨框架互操作、复杂工作流的委派协作、安全不透明的 agent 交互，以及通过正式扩展维持核心稳定的工程机制上。四个面向共同构成 A2A 相对既有 agent 集成方案的核心差异。

1: # A2A Protocol
2: 
3: Agent2Agent Protocol Logo
4: -------------------------
5: 
6: An open protocol enabling communication and interoperability between opaque agentic applications.
7: 
8: An open standard enabling users to connect agents to tools and data through MCP, and to other agents through A2A.
9: 
10: An open standard enabling developers to expose portable tools through MCP and interoperable agents through A2A.
11: 
12: What is A2A Protocol?[¶](#what-is-a2a-protocol "Permanent link")
13: ----------------------------------------------------------------
14: 
15: The **Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol** is an open standard for seamless communication and collaboration between AI agents. In a world where agents are built using diverse frameworks and by different vendors, A2A provides the definitive common language for agent interoperability.
16: 
17: Build with
18: **[![ADK Logo](https://adk.dev/assets/agent-development-kit.png) ADK](https://adk.dev/)** *(or any framework)*,
19: equip with **[![MCP Logo](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/mcp.png) MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)** *(or any tool)*,
20: and communicate with
21: **![A2A Logo](assets/a2a_logo/icon/color/SVG/a2a_icon_color.svg) A2A**,
22: to remote agents, local agents, and humans.
23: 
24: Key Features[¶](#key-features "Permanent link")
25: -----------------------------------------------
26: 
27: * **Interoperability**
28: 
29:   Connect agents built on different platforms (LangGraph, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, custom solutions) to create powerful, composite AI systems.
30: * **Complex Workflows**
31: 
32:   Enable agents to delegate sub-tasks, exchange information, and coordinate actions to solve complex problems that a single agent cannot.
33: * **Secure & Opaque**
34: 
35:   Agents interact without needing to share internal memory, tools, or proprietary logic, ensuring security and preserving intellectual property.
36: * **Extensible**
37: 
38:   Add capabilities through formal protocol [extensions and custom bindings](topics/extension-and-binding-governance/), governed by a tiered promotion process so the core stays stable.
39: 
40: Get started with A2A[¶](#get-started-with-a2a "Permanent link")

1: # A2A and MCP - A2A Protocol
2: 
3: A2A and MCP: Detailed Comparison[¶](#a2a-and-mcp-detailed-comparison "Permanent link")
4: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5: 
6: In AI agent development, two key protocol types emerge to facilitate
7: interoperability. One connects agents to tools and resources. The other enables
8: agent-to-agent collaboration. The Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol and the
9: [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP) address these distinct but highly complementary needs.
10: 
11: Horizontal and Vertical Layers[¶](#horizontal-and-vertical-layers "Permanent link")
12: -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
13: 
14: One way to picture the two protocols is by the direction they connect in.
15: 
16: **MCP is vertical.** It deepens a single agent. You can build an agentic system
17: under one roof — one or more agents in a single application. Every MCP connection
18: you add hands an agent another tool, resource, or skill. The more you connect,
19: the more that agent can do on its own.
20: 
21: **A2A is horizontal.** It connects agents across that boundary. The other agent
22: may belong to another team, another department, or a partner organization. Your
23: agent reaches out to those agents to discover them, negotiate, and exchange
24: information.
25: 
26: That horizontal reach goes beyond asking another agent for a status update. It is
27: closer to how one person reaches out to another for help: *"Are you working on
28: this project? Do you know about it? Can you share what you have — and if not,
29: which agent can?"* Agents break the ice, exchange context, and — depending on how
30: the exchange goes — either go deeper or get pointed to a better place to get the
31: job done.
32: 
33: Used together, MCP gives each agent depth, and A2A gives your system reach.
34: 
35: Model Context Protocol[¶](#model-context-protocol "Permanent link")
36: -------------------------------------------------------------------
37: 
38: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) defines how an AI agent uses individual tools and resources, such as a database or an API.
39: 
40: This protocol offers the following capabilities:
41: 
42: * Standardizes how AI models and agents connect to and interact with tools,
43:   APIs, and other external resources.
44: * Defines a structured way to describe tool capabilities, similar to function
45:   calling in Large Language Models.
46: * Passes inputs to tools and receives structured outputs.
47: * Supports common use cases, such as an LLM calling an external API, an agent
48:   querying a database, or an agent connecting to predefined functions.
49: 
50: Agent2Agent Protocol[¶](#agent2agent-protocol "Permanent link")
51: ---------------------------------------------------------------
52: 
53: The Agent2Agent Protocol lets different agents collaborate to reach a common goal.
54: 
55: This protocol offers the following capabilities:
56: 
57: * Standardizes how independent, often opaque, AI agents communicate and
58:   collaborate as peers.
59: * Gives agents an application-level protocol. With it, agents discover each
60:   other and negotiate interactions. They also manage shared tasks and exchange
61:   conversational context and complex data.
62: * Supports common use cases. For example, a customer service agent might delegate
63:   an inquiry to a billing agent. A travel agent might coordinate with flight,
64:   hotel, and activity agents.
65: 
66: Why Different Protocols?[¶](#why-different-protocols "Permanent link")
67: ----------------------------------------------------------------------
68: 
69: Both protocols are essential for building complex AI systems. The distinction between A2A and MCP depends on what an agent interacts with.
70: 
71: * **Tools and Resources (MCP Domain)**:
72:   + **Characteristics:** These are typically primitives with well-defined,
73:     structured inputs and outputs. They perform specific, often stateless,
74:     functions. Examples include a calculator, a database query API, or a
75:     weather lookup service.
76:   + **Purpose:** Agents use tools to gather information and perform discrete
77:     functions.
78: * **Agents (A2A domain)**:
79:   + **Characteristics:** These are more autonomous systems. They reason,
80:     plan, and use multiple tools. They keep state over longer interactions
81:     and hold complex, often multi-turn dialogues to handle novel or evolving
82:     tasks.
83:   + **Purpose:** Agents collaborate with other agents to tackle broader, more
84:     complex goals.
85: 
86: A2A ❤️ MCP: Complementary Protocols for Agentic Systems[¶](#a2a-mcp-complementary-protocols-for-agentic-systems "Permanent link")
87: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
88: 
89: An agentic application might use A2A to communicate with other agents. Inside,
90: each agent uses MCP to work with its own tools and resources.
91: 
92: ![Diagram showing A2A and MCP working together. A User interacts with Agent A using A2A. Agent A interacts with Agent B using A2A. Agent B uses MCP to interact with Tool 1 and Tool 2.](../../assets/a2a-mcp.png)
93: 
94: *A2A connects the agents to each other; MCP connects each agent to its own tools.*
95: 
96: ### Example Scenario: The Auto Repair Shop[¶](#example-scenario-the-auto-repair-shop "Permanent link")
97: 
98: Consider an auto repair shop staffed by autonomous AI agent "mechanics".
99: These mechanics diagnose and repair problems with special-purpose tools. Their
100: tools include vehicle diagnostic scanners, repair manuals, and platform lifts.
101: The repair process can involve long conversations, research, and work with part
102: suppliers.
103: 
104: * **Customer interaction — user-to-agent via A2A.** A customer, or their
105:   assistant agent, talks to the "Shop Manager" agent.
106: 
107:   For example, the customer might say, "My car is making a rattling noise".
108: * **Diagnostic conversation — agent-to-agent via A2A.** The Shop Manager agent
109:   holds a back-and-forth diagnostic conversation.
110: 
111:   For example, the Manager might ask, "Can you send a video of the noise?" or "I see some fluid leaking. How long has this been happening?".
112: * **Internal tool use — agent-to-tool via MCP.** The Mechanic agent, assigned
113:   the task by the Shop Manager, needs to diagnose the issue. It uses MCP to
114:   reach its specialized tools.
115: 
116:   For example:
117: 
118:   + MCP call to a "Vehicle Diagnostic Scanner" tool:
119:     `scan_vehicle_for_error_codes(vehicle_id='XYZ123')`
120:   + MCP call to a "Repair Manual Database" tool:
121:     `get_repair_procedure(error_code='P0300', vehicle_make='Toyota',
122:     vehicle_model='Camry')`
123:   + MCP call to a "Platform Lift" tool: `raise_platform(height_meters=2)`
124: * **Supplier interaction — agent-to-agent via A2A.** The Mechanic agent finds
125:   that a specific part is needed. It uses A2A to talk to a "Parts Supplier"
126:   agent and order the part.
127:   For example, the
128:   Mechanic agent might ask, "Do you have part #12345 in stock for a Toyota Camry 2018?"
129: * **Order processing — agent-to-agent via A2A.** The Parts Supplier agent is
130:   also an A2A-compliant system. It responds, which can lead to an order.
131: 
132: In this example:
133: 
134: * A2A handles the higher-level, conversational, task-oriented interactions. It
135:   links the customer with the shop, and the shop's agents with outside supplier
136:   agents.
137: * MCP enables the mechanic agent to use its specific, structured tools to
138:   perform its diagnostic and repair functions.
139:

**异构 agent 的统一互操作标准。** 在由不同框架、不同厂商构建的 agent 生态中，A2A 为 seamless agent 互操作提供通用语言。世界上的 agent 采用多样的框架并由不同厂商构建，A2A 正是为了给这种异构环境提供统一的通信标准 [S1]。

**复杂问题的多 agent 协同。** 单一 agent 无法解决所有复杂问题，因此需要多 agent 委派子任务、交换信息、协调行动。A2A 使 agent 能够委派子任务、交换信息并协调行动，以解决单个 agent 无法完成的复杂问题 [S1]。这种协作常常跨越组织边界——另一个 agent 可能属于另一个团队、部门或伙伴组织，你的 agent 需要向外发现它们、进行协商并交换信息 [S4]。修车厂示例直观地展示了这一能力：客户通过 A2A 与 Shop Manager agent 对话，Shop Manager 与 Mechanic agent 委派诊断任务，Mechanic 再通过 A2A 与外部 Parts Supplier agent 协商下单 [S4]。

**协作中安全不透明的保护。** agent 之间协作时，双方无需暴露内部记忆、工具或专有逻辑，从而保证安全性并保护知识产权。这正是 "Secure & Opaque" 的设计取向 [S1]。

**作为互补层填补 agent 到 agent 通信空档。** MCP 是垂直的，它加深单个 agent，让 agent 连接自己的工具与资源；A2A 是水平的，它在边界之外连接 agent 与 agent [S4]。两者互补：MCP 让每个 agent 有深度，A2A 让整个系统有广度 [S4]。修车厂示例显示，Mechanic agent 内部用 MCP 调用诊断扫描仪、维修手册、升降机等工具，而 Shop Manager、Mechanic 与 Parts Supplier 之间通过 A2A 对话 [S4]。因此 A2A 填补了 MCP 仅覆盖 agent 到工具、而不覆盖 agent 到 agent 通信的这一层空档。

综合以上各节，A2A 与 MCP 可以被归结为两类互补的互联问题：MCP 解决的是 **agent 到工具**，A2A 解决的是 **agent 到 agent**。二者并非竞争对手，而是被设计成协同工作的两层协议 [S1]。MCP 标准化了单个 agent 接入其工具、API 与资源以获取信息的连接方式；而 A2A 作为通用的去中心化标准，让彼此独立（包括使用 MCP 的）的 agent 能够互相发现、委派任务并共享结果 [S1]。在 AI agent 开发中，这两类协议分别聚焦"连接 agent 与工具/资源"和"实现 agent 之间的协作"，处理的是不同但高度互补的需求 [S4]。

**关于差异与联系。** 二者的分工清晰：MCP 装备单个 agent 以完成其任务所需的具体工具（如访问 GitHub 仓库或 SQL 数据库），而 A2A 让这些专门的 agent 跨不同框架安全地协作 [S1]。因此联系在于它们处于同一 agent 体系的不同层面，实际部署中常常协同使用——MCP 负责横向打通 agent 与工具，A2A 负责纵向打通 agent 与 agent。

**关于创新之处。** A2A 的主要创新体现在三方面：一是作为开放的去中心化标准实现**跨框架互操作**，使来自不同厂商的异构 agent 能在统一规范下互联；二是支持**复杂工作流**的编排与委派，agent 之间可以相互发现、传递任务与共享结果 [S1]；三是其**安全与不透明机制**，允许 agent 在协作过程中按需保护内部信息，同时保持协作的安全边界。

**关于要解决的问题。** A2A 专门针对当前生态中的空档——既有协议（如 MCP）只解决了 agent 与工具之间的互联，缺少一个标准化的、面向**异构 agent 互操作**的层；A2A 着力填补多供应商、多框架环境下 agent 无法直接协作的空档，同时解决**多 agent 协作**时的发现、委派、结果共享，以及**协作安全**问题。整体上，A2A 是专为多厂商异构 agent 的互操作与协作需求而设计的互补方案 [S1][S4]。
